Henry intended to bake twice as many cookies as he did last year. Let \( L \) be the number of cookies he baked last year. His intended amount was \( 2L \). He actually baked 15 more than intended, so he baked \( 2L + 15 \) cookies. After dropping 5 cookies, he has \( (2L + 15) - 5 = 2L + 10 \) cookies left. This equals 110 cookies:

\[
2L + 10 = 110
\]
\[
2L = 100
\]
\[
L = 50
\]

Answer: 50
